chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Abū Ayyūb, from Yazīd al-Kunāsī, who said:
I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a woman who married during her waiting period.

He said: «If she married during a divorce waiting period in which her husband had the right of الرجعة, then upon her is stoning. If she married during a waiting period in which her husband had no right of الرجعة, then upon her is the punishment of an unmarried fornicator. And if she married during the waiting period after her husband's death, before the completion of four months and ten days, then there is no stoning upon her, but upon her is one hundred lashes.»

I said: What if she did that out of ignorance? He said: «There is no woman today among the Muslim women except that she knows that she must observe a waiting period after divorce or death, and indeed the women of the Jāhiliyyah used to know that.»

I said: Then what if she knows that she must observe a waiting period, but does not know how long it is? He said: «If she knows that the waiting period is upon her, then the proof is binding upon her, so she must ask until she comes to know.»

key_terms.الرَّجْعَةُ: the husband's right to take back his wife during a revocable divorce waiting period
key_terms.الرَّجْمَ: the legal punishment of stoning in the specified case
key_terms.الْأَرْبَعَةِ أَشْهُرٍ وَالْعَشَرَةِ أَي: the duration of the waiting period after a husband's death
key_terms.الْحُجَّةُ: the binding proof or established responsibility before Allah
key_terms.حَدَّ الزَّانِي غَيْرِ الْمُحْصَنِ: the prescribed punishment of an unmarried fornicator
key_terms.عِدَّتِهَا: her legally required waiting period after divorce or death of a husband

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a woman who marries during her ʿiddah in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings for a woman who marries during her ʿiddah, distinguishing between revocable divorce, irrevocable separation, and the waiting period after her husband's death. It also states that awareness of the obligation of ʿiddah establishes responsibility, and ignorance of its exact duration does not excuse one from asking and learning the ruling.
